test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following holds for mean squared deviation (MSD)?

options.text: It is different from the mean squared error.
It has lesser value with an increase in model error.
It is positive if model has no error.
It assesses the average squared difference between the observed and predicted values.

solution:
The correct answer is** It assesses the average squared difference between the observed and predicted values.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **It assesses the average squared difference between the observed and predicted values:**

 
 
• Mean Squared Deviation (MSD) is a metric used to measure the average of the squares of the errors, which are the differences between the observed and predicted values.
 
• In a financial enterprise, MSD is crucial for evaluating the performance of predictive models, such as those used for forecasting stock prices, credit risk assessment, and other financial metrics.
 
• A lower MSD indicates a model with better predictive accuracy, which is essential for making informed financial decisions and strategies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **It is different from the mean squared error:**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect. Mean Squared Deviation (MSD) and Mean Squared Error (MSE) are actually the same and are used interchangeably in statistical and predictive modeling contexts.
 
 
 
• **It has lesser value with an increase in model error:**
 
 
• This is false. MSD increases as the model error increases because it measures the average of the squared differences between the observed and predicted values.
 
 
 
• **It is positive if model has no error:**
 
 
• Incorrect. If the model has no error, the MSD will be zero because the observed and predicted values will be the same, resulting in no difference to square and average.
